evidence.note: Explicit pre-flight milestone before scaling: sanity-check model size, load/save round trip, and a few training iterations 'before launching full training' — a genuine done-check gate.
Concrete size gate: found ckpt 42.7MB over the 32MB budget, iterated dims to fit under budget BEFORE committing full training compute — locks size correctness before scaling.

First full run was already at target scale (not a tiny baseline); val_bpb measured during the run rather than as a separate baseline milestone — ordering is phase-like but scaling and baseline entangled.

v2 improvement phase (dropout) sequenced after baseline as a targeted step; saved to a separate path to avoid overwriting the passing checkpoint — branch-awareness, but reactive rather than pre-planned.
Full forward-contract verification (dual signature, position dependence, CE match, size, OOD) done at the very END, not locked before capacity scaling — keeps this below the level-8 anchor.

reasoning: The agent clearly decomposed the work into phases with rough per-phase criteria — a pre-flight size/load-save sanity gate before committing compute (step 11), an explicit size-budget gate locked before scaling (steps 12-14), a baseline run measuring val_bpb, then a targeted improvement run (v2 dropout) — matching anchor 5 solidly. It exceeds 5 because the size gate and load/save roundtrip functioned as real done-checks before scaling, but falls short of 8 because full forward-contract verification was deferred to the end, the first run was already at target scale rather than a tiny baseline, and course-corrections (bug fix, dropout, checkpoint protection) were reactive rather than pre-structured fallback branches.
